LAREDO, Texas — Texas A&M International University is going all-in on student health next week with “Wicked Wellness Week 2026,” a five-day campus initiative running Monday, Oct. 26 through Friday, Oct. 30, according to TAMIU’s newsroom.

The week blends preventive, behavioral, and mental health programming under playful Halloween-themed branding. Standout events include a weeklong flu vaccine pop-in (students who get vaccinated at Student Health Services score a free t-shirt while supplies last), an alcohol-awareness session on Oct. 26, and a two-day campus blood drive Oct. 27–28 held with the South Texas Blood and Tissue Center.

NARCAN training with the city

On Tuesday, Oct. 27, the university partners with the City of Laredo Health Department for NARCAN training and distribution, teaching students to recognize the signs of an opioid overdose and when and how to administer the nasal spray. The first 80 students to register also get free lunch.

Wednesday’s “Zero Gravity, Zero Stigma” session puts College of Nursing and Health Sciences students front and center on substance use and recovery. The week closes with the annual Halloween Fest on Thursday, Oct. 29 (6–9 p.m., Zaffirini Student Success Center Green) — a family-friendly fundraiser for student organizations featuring food, games, a costume contest, a pumpkin patch, trick-or-treating, inflatables, and a haunted house. The blood drive and Halloween Fest are open to the public.

Sources: Texas A&M International University newsroom (Oct. 22, 2026).

title: TAMIU launches 'Wicked Wellness Week' Oct. 26–30 with NARCAN training, blood drive, public Halloween Fest
